Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: Speakers who rehearse with note cards can remember the order of their main points. Which paraphrase is most accurate?

answer.text: A. Speakers should never use note cards because they distract the audience.

feedback.text: This changes the meaning. The source says note cards can help speakers remember order.

answer.text: B. Main points are not important when a speaker rehearses.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source. The source connects note cards to remembering main points.

answer.text: C. Practicing with note cards can help speakers keep their main points in order.

feedback.text: Correct. This restates the source meaning in new wording without changing the idea.

answer.text: D. Note cards are only useful for writing essays.

feedback.text: This adds an unrelated idea and moves away from speech notes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.03

Source: Clear transitions help listeners understand how one point connects to the next. What is the key meaning?

answer.text: A. Listeners do not need transitions.

feedback.text: This reverses the source meaning. The source says transitions help listeners.

answer.text: B. Speakers should avoid connecting points.

feedback.text: This is the opposite of the source idea.

answer.text: C. Transitions are only used in written essays.

feedback.text: The source is about listeners and speech points, not only essays.

answer.text: D. Transitions help the audience follow relationships between speech points.

feedback.text: Correct. This captures the important meaning of the source sentence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.05

Which academic word should probably stay in a paraphrase about speech preparation?

answer.text: A. audience

feedback.text: Correct. Audience is a precise communication term and may be needed for accuracy.

answer.text: B. stuff

feedback.text: This is vague and not academic vocabulary.

answer.text: C. things

feedback.text: This is general and does not make the paraphrase precise.

answer.text: D. whatever

feedback.text: This is informal and not appropriate academic vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Source: A concise speech note reminds the speaker of an idea without requiring a full sentence. Which speech note best paraphrases the idea?

answer.text: A. A concise speech note reminds the speaker of an idea without requiring a full sentence.

feedback.text: This copies the source exactly, so it is not a paraphrase.

answer.text: B. Short note: remember idea, do not read full sentence.

feedback.text: Correct. This keeps the meaning and changes it into a usable speech note.

answer.text: C. Full sentences are always required on note cards.

feedback.text: This changes the meaning because the source says a full sentence is not required.

answer.text: D. Notes should include every word of the speech.

feedback.text: This contradicts the source and would not support natural speaking.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L03_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.05

Which action is part of strong paraphrasing?

answer.text: A. Replace one word at a time and keep the same sentence structure.

feedback.text: This is too close to copying and does not show full paraphrasing.

answer.text: B. Add a new opinion that was not in the source.

feedback.text: This changes the source meaning and makes the paraphrase inaccurate.

answer.text: C. Understand the meaning, then restate it with new wording and structure.

feedback.text: Correct. Strong paraphrasing begins with meaning and then restates accurately.

answer.text: D. Remove the main idea so the sentence is shorter.

feedback.text: Shorter is not better if the important meaning is lost.
